title: Inverse image under the fixed finite discrete coefficient encoding
statement: For B, eR and G of [def-weil-pbc-common-finite-discrete-encoding], every scheme morphism j:U→T and every internal coefficient module M on T admit an isomorphism between j-star(E_T.inverse M) and E_U.inverse of the internal inverse image of M, normalized by restriction of scalars along the inverse coefficient pullback isomorphism. No finiteness or discreteness hypothesis on B is required.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.2 and Lemmas 5.4.1 and 5.4.3; Stacks Project Tag 09AK

proof.text: Expand the section action of the encoding as the coefficient-unit map followed by the underlying internal action. The direct-image tensor identity and coefficient-unit compatibility make the two actions equal on every section. This gives a sectionwise module isomorphism, natural in the module.

Restrict the direct-image comparison to sheaves and conjugate through the encoding equivalences. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the ordinary and internal inverse images. Along the invertible coefficient pullback, extension of scalars equals restriction along its inverse.

theorem finiteDiscreteCoefficient_restrictionEncoding
    (T U : Scheme.{u}) (j : U ⟶ T) (M : FiniteDiscreteInternalModules B T) :
    Nonempty (
      ((j)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} B)]).obj
        ((finiteDiscreteCoefficientEquivalence B eR G hG T).inverse.obj M) ≅
      (finiteDiscreteCoefficientEquivalence B eR G hG U).inverse.obj
        ((Mod.comap (inv (condensedPullbackHom
          (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B) j))).obj
          ((((j)^*[Ab.{u + 1}]).mapMod
            (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B) T)).obj M)))
